rationale: Ground truth's only substantive points are (1) whether attrgetter is overkill outside the dotted-path case and (2) that this mirrors module_collector.py's existing dotted-path resolution pattern, suggesting a shared helper. Y explicitly hits both — it cites ModuleDiscovery._collect_modules/module_collector.py as the precedent this PR mirrors and proposes a similar warning-log helper, and its closing note independently confirms attrgetter is only necessary for dotted names, echoing the human back-and-forth. X never mentions module_collector.py or the necessity question at all. Both candidates independently surface a well-grounded, previously-unflagged SoulX Singer cache-activation risk with specific file:line evidence, giving both decent precision, but Y's analysis is deeper (DBCache sequence-length mechanism, is_cached guard vs cache_dit's actual no-op behavior) and pairs more of its findings with concrete suggested code. X's report is still solid and actionable but misses the two things the actual reviewers cared about.
